name: Trade war & tariffs
value: Mexico doubling threat 12 Nov; none in force
summary: Trump's threat to double tariffs on Mexico has not been enacted; a US–Philippines trade deal was announced on 18 Nov
state: President Trump threatened on 12 Nov to double tariffs on Mexico over a migrant caravan, and President Sheinbaum said caravans would not reach the US border (KJZZ). Mexican goods outside USMCA face a 10% duty, and steel, aluminium and cars 25–50% (Rio Times). On 18 Nov Trump announced a trade deal with the Philippines, with no tariff terms published (Philstar). Searches to 20 Nov found no new tariff increase in force and no retaliation, so Watch holds.
for_you: Importers, exporters and manufacturers with US–Mexico supply chains, notably in cars and metals, are the most exposed if the threatened increase takes effect. Prices of imported goods tend to follow tariff changes with a lag.
rubric_hit: Watch: major new tariffs threatened between large economies (US threat to double Mexico tariffs, 12 Nov); none in force, no retaliation

sources.title: KJZZ — Sheinbaum says migrant caravans will not reach U.S.-Mexico border as Trump threatens higher tariffs

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
